verse.reading: The form, the self, youth, the daughter, the mother, the mother-in-law and those who took the ground: in a town, is it justice to celebrate blame? Is the newcomer a pauper, is the potter a dwarf, is the one standing in the middle an idler? The city has been plundered.
verse.nuance: The verse is obscure and reads as cipher. நகரம் சூறையானது, the city has been looted, is read by tradition as the body-city plundered by death or by the senses, with the potter (குயவன்) as Brahma who shaped it and the one standing in the middle (நடுநின்றான்) as the soul or the Lord within; on that reading the household figures of line 1 are the body's attachments. A plain reading of a town's quarrel and its sack is possible but gives no connected sense. Every part of the reading given is doubtful.

finding.claim: Ageing reflects a set of interacting cellular hallmarks such as genomic instability, loss of protein balance and stem-cell exhaustion, none yet reversed in humans.

verse.reading: I became a painted picture, water on red-hot iron; and I knew the awareness that calls the state where all is level 'sleep'.
verse.nuance: தெத்தபடம் is obscure (perhaps தத்தப்படம், a picture or screen, a mere image); the iron image repeats 615. ஒத்த இடம் நித்திரை may mean that the state of evenness beyond waking and dream is what the traditions call sleep, or that for her it is indistinguishable from sleep; the line turns on technical words of the avastha scheme.

finding.claim: A microtubule-stabilising drug delayed isoflurane-induced unconsciousness in rats, consistent with but not proof of a microtubule role in consciousness.

verse.reading: What is sent goes to the uvula and the palate, sir; climbing there, meditation appears by the way of the nape; the four have grown strong and become nectar for you; it has become the life called silence, without distinctions; hold it in the twelve where it sounds, and blow; the sixteen-fold digit of the moon has waned away; the siddhi of yoga and the siddhi of knowledge have borne fruit; in due season set the channel and make it practice.
verse.nuance: The tongue or breath sent to உண்ணாக்கு, அண்ணாக்கு (uvula, palate) is the khechari practice, from which nectar is said to flow. மவுனம் is here redefined as நிருவிகற்பம், the state without distinctions, reached through breath and not instead of it, answering 2457. சோடசமாம் சந்த்ரகலை தேய்ந்து போச்சு, the sixteen-fold moon has waned, is ambiguous: the moon's nectar consumed by the yogi, or the moon-breath exhausted. The four that grew strong are unexplained.

finding.claim: The idea that a fixed stock of breaths or heartbeats sets lifespan rests on a cross-species correlation; within humans, lower resting heart rate predicts lower mortality but slowing breath has not been shown to extend life.

verse.reading: Are there firm gains without toil, or helplessness that does not come from failing to toil? So dig the stump of deceit root and all out of the field of the heart, clear it, lay out the bed called love, spread the manure called truth, plant the single seed of doubtless devotion, water it daily with the clear water of ardour, and fearing the five cattle that break in past every guard, go in and build the fence of peace; then the great sprout of knowledge rises, shows the tender shoot of compassion, the weeds of lust and anger are pulled, it grows straight, the hair bristles, tears bud, the fragrant flower opens and the rare fruit of the five letters appears, with poison throat, three eyes, eight shoulders, five bright faces, coral colour and white ash, sweeter than the six tastes, a joy to see, hear and think of; the ruby fruit of high Marudur ripens slowly into the hand, and our kind eat it and hold their heads high. Some do not come this way: they make the field of the mind a waste, let the forest of lust cover it where the hunters of the five senses rob, chase the mirage-chariot of pleasure that is never reached, the deer of untaught sense wanders, and when the seed of desire is dropped the great poison tree called 'I' shoots up, puts out branches of lies, spreads leaves of sin, buds cruelty, flowers harshness, hangs fruit of sorrow, ripens death and falls into the serpent's place: useless to themselves and others, they pass in the blink of an eye; such is their nature.
verse.nuance: The allegory is worked out stage by stage on both sides, cultivation and neglect, and the two trees are the Lord (the five-letter fruit wearing his own iconography) and the ego (யான் எனப் பெயரிய நச்சு மாமரம், the poison tree named 'I'). The five cattle and the five hunters are the senses in both halves. நாகிடை வீழ்ந்து, falling among the serpent, probably means hell; a variant reading is not recorded.

finding.claim: Quantum cognition uses the mathematics of quantum probability to model order effects and violations of classical probability in human judgment; it makes no claim that brains are quantum devices.

verse.reading: In the way of Paychalur, in the whirl where the Supreme dwelt, at the tip of the ripening horn, on the mountain where the fruit is: what is it that smells so? The expanse rests here; the light that stands pressing, drawing breath from breath.
verse.nuance: பாய்ச்சலூர், the town of leaping or flowing, recurs in 1328 and 1333 and is cipher for the breath's course or the central channel, as tradition takes it, not a place. மூச்சினோடு மூச்சை வாங்கு, drawing breath by breath, is the one plain phrase. The question ஏதடா asks what the fragrance or stench at the fruit is.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of small randomised trials finds alternate-nostril breathing lowers blood pressure modestly, with high heterogeneity between studies.

verse.reading: Going through the sky, child, the wheel spun and danced; mounting the wheel without slipping I went beyond it; going a long way I surely saw the state of the pillar; it stands spread like fire, and no space or anything else could be seen.
verse.nuance: சக்கரம் here is the spinning wheel of the cosmos or of the crown, which the seer rides past; கம்பம், the pillar of fire, is Siva as the lingodbhava column, the form in which neither Brahma nor Vishnu could find his ends.

finding.claim: The insula integrates signals from inside the body into a felt sense of bodily state, and disturbed interoception is implicated in anxiety, depression and eating disorders.

verse.reading: I will speak: the left channel is the moonstone; the right channel is the sun from the first; when the light that stood lovingly in the middle departs and then becomes one without departing, that is release; for those who looked with love, this is moksha here; for those who do not see, what is there but a body of lust? As a test, draw the breath up in the left channel, hold it in the sushumna, and you will be entranced.
verse.nuance: The cipher is stated and then decoded within the verse: இடைகலை is the moon, பின்கலை the sun, and the middle light the sushumna where they unite. சோதனையாய், as a test, invites the hearer to try the kumbhaka and see; சொக்குவீரே (you will be stunned, or absorbed) is the promised result.

finding.claim: Quantum cognition uses the mathematics of quantum probability to model order effects and violations of classical probability in human judgment; it makes no claim that brains are quantum devices.

verse.reading: Fire says 'it is mine', the worm says 'mine', this earth says 'mine', the kite says 'mine, to eat', the jackal says 'mine', the base dog says 'mine': this stinking body I reared with love, and what gain do I have from it?
verse.nuance: The six claimants are the six ends of a corpse: cremation, decay, burial, and the scavengers of the burning ground. The verse's bite is in பிரியமுடன் வளர்த்தேன், that the poet fed with love what was never his but already spoken for.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: It tells of the guru who is the place where pati is; do not open it in public, your head will split in two; listen as I say what place fate is: it is the uvula within the sky of the sky; moon and sun, pooranam, eye, mouth, nose, the great ear and touch, eight; the place where pati dwells, its name is the suzhumunai; they call it heaven and Kailasa.
verse.nuance: The verse names the place three ways: the uvula within the inner sky, the suzhumunai, and heaven and Kailasa, which 2439 expands into a list of all the holy places. The eight (moon, sun, pooranam and the five senses) is another of the run's counts. விதியின்ன விடம், 'the place where fate is', is strange; a variant sense is 'the place as ordained'. The threat that the head splits in two for telling it openly is a conventional curse on breaking secrecy.

verse.reading: For the kalpa you need not go far, nor wander the peaks of stone mountains; standing on the head of the serpent called the naga, find the undying breath, climb to the tip, stand in a mind made firm by resolve, and see the true juice of the black gooseberry; if you drop it as a small thing you will wander lost; go and join the Supreme called turiya.
verse.nuance: கற்பம் is the rejuvenating herb or preparation of Siddha medicine; the verse says it is not gathered in the mountains but found within. The sense turns on cipher: tradition takes the serpent as kundalini at the base, சாகாத கால் (the undying foot or breath) as the breath that does not go out, and கருநெல்லிச் சாறு (black-gooseberry juice) as the nectar from the head; Kakapusundar uses the same herb-name for the deathless state. A plain medical reading, that gooseberry juice is the kalpa, is also possible and the verse plays on both.

finding.claim: Trained practitioners of breathing and cold exposure or of tummo meditation can voluntarily raise body temperature or modulate the innate immune response, effects once thought impossible.

verse.reading: At sixteen he has the teaching of a guru of lofty wisdom and the arts of Tamil to their shore, is praised as a waxing moon, dresses his hair with flowers that bees hum round, wears gold and gems and is bowed to by bards; women see him as Kama's form, crowd and throw their curved glances, and when they go like peacocks he runs after them, embraces, drinks the nectar of their lips and gives away the whole capital he had gathered; the hoarded wealth is lost to idleness, and calling this the pleasure and grief of Kama he parts from the youthful form; prosperity and youth change, the strong teeth fall, the two eyes darken, age ripens, grey hair and wrinkles come with wind, quarrel and anger, and a staff is in his red hand.
verse.nuance: Learning and wealth are given to the youth only so that the women can strip them; the stanza does not call the women courtesans, but தேடிய மாமுதல் சேர வழங்கி (giving away all the capital he had sought) is the courtesan verses' plot. வாதவிரோதகுரோதம் can be read as the wind-disease of old age or as quarrelsomeness; தடி (staff) and நரைதிரை are the standard marks of age.

finding.claim: Whether adult humans make new hippocampal neurons is disputed, with major studies reporting both near-absence and abundance.

verse.reading: Chewing, swallowing, then seeking water to put out the thirst: when will the dawn come for me, my King, Marudha who burned the three cities of those who did not think on the good, now that I have come to your presence?
verse.nuance: The round of eating and drinking stands for the whole of embodied life, and என்று விடியும், when will it dawn, makes that life a night. The verse asks the Lord of Idaimarudur for release from the body's needs, not for food.

finding.claim: Intermittent fasting improves metabolic markers in animals and some humans, but trials show weight loss similar to ordinary calorie restriction.

verse.reading: He of unchanging fame and the honey garland, the Siva-yogi of silence who does not open his mouth to rage; and straight (2197) his guru is Chitrambalavan.
verse.nuance: வாய்திறந்து சீறாத: silence is defined as not opening the mouth in anger, a narrower and more practical mounam than the stilling of all thought. Yet 2194 gave him fury; the anger is turned on the disciples' enemies, not spoken.

tamil: ஒழிந்த கருத்தினை வைத்து உள் எலும்பு வெள் எலும்பாய்க்
கழிந்த பிணம் போல் இருந்து காண்பது இனி எக்காலம்?
verse.reading: When will I keep the thought that has ceased, lie like a discarded corpse with the inner bone turned white bone, and see?
verse.nuance: ஒழிந்த கருத்து is thought that has stopped, or the one thought that remains when the rest have gone; the near-double at 23 has ஒழிந்த தருமம் instead. வெள் எலும்பு, the bone bleached white, is the corpse long dead; the poet asks to lie as one while still seeing (காண்பது), the living death of 89 and 139.

finding.claim: Elemental, inorganic and organic mercury are toxic to the nervous system and kidneys, and no safe therapeutic role for ingested mercury is established.

verse.reading: The good light is the light of knowledge; the light that is no light, Jnanam, mother, is a base light.
verse.nuance: இல்லா வெளிச்சம், 'the light that is not', may be the light of the senses and the world, which is not true light and so is low; or it may be read as 'the light that is not there', the dark. The plain claim is that only the light of jnana is good.

finding.claim: Meditators report a wide range of challenging experiences, including perceived lights, altered self-sense, fear and lasting distress, some needing support.

verse.reading: When will the mind that will not settle settle, and when will I see the house of bliss and stay there gazing without blinking?
verse.nuance: இமையாமல் நோக்கி, the unblinking gaze, is a mark of the yogic trance in the tradition; the house (வீடு) is release. The settling of the mind comes first and the seeing follows.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: Setting my mind unmoving in the great awareness, when will I stand rooted every day in the one awareness?
verse.nuance: பேரறிவு and ஓரறிவு, the great awareness and the one awareness, are the same thing named from two sides: its size and its singleness.

finding.claim: Much meditation research suffers from vague definitions, small samples and overstated claims, and the evidence for its benefits is weaker than popular accounts suggest.

verse.reading: Before conception, where did the body stand? Before it took form, where did the breath of life stand? In the thought wrapped in confusion, where did delusion stand? Jnanis who have come to know what you desired, you must explain this at length.
verse.nuance: Three questions on origins, each ending எவ்விடம் (where), put as a challenge to professed jnanis. The verse does not answer them; whether it means the answers are unknowable or that they are the test of real knowledge is left open.

finding.claim: The gut microbiota signals to the brain through immune, endocrine and vagal routes and affects stress responses and behaviour in animals; human causal evidence is still limited.

verse.reading: Is not the fit true learning the learning learned in order to be silent? Work it out, stony mind.
verse.nuance: Learning has silence as its end, not speech or debate; வாகான, fitting or well-formed, marks this as the true kind among the learnings of 1794.

finding.claim: A theoretical account proposes that meditation progressively loosens predictive models, from reduced mind-wandering to cessation of experience in advanced states.

verse.reading: Whether sitting or walking, raise the essences without letting them go through other talk; four or eight, all is one; in the good eight-limbed practice, the siddhi of practice; if you first do pranayama as the measure, by count the filling and the holding are four, the emptying one and three; without shortfall join the sarabhi and finish.
verse.nuance: The verse gives a counted pranayama, but the ratio is garbled: பூரகம் கும்பகம் நாலு, ரேசகம் ஒன்று மூன்று may be the standard 1:4:2 with a number lost. சரபீ (also 2463, சரபீசம்) is unexplained; it may be a seed-syllable or a name for the combined breath. The claim that four and eight are all one is probably that the fourfold and eightfold yogas reduce to breath.

finding.claim: Breathing voluntarily at about six breaths a minute raises vagally mediated heart-rate variability during practice, right after one session and after multi-session training.

verse.reading: To speak this lament, the word of knowledge that gives release, when shall I receive the grace of the elephant-faced one?
verse.nuance: An invocation to Ganapati (அத்திமுகவன், the elephant-faced) outside the work's own numbering; it names the whole poem a புலம்பல் (lament) and claims that its words give release.

finding.claim: Placebos given openly, with patients told they are inert, still produce moderate improvements in self-reported symptoms.

verse.reading: My belly boils like a smith's forge; when I say 'stop' I cannot make it stand still; and if I could say 'stop' and hold it still, would not Death, who came saying 'kill', flee with his household, my Mother?
verse.nuance: The boiling belly is read as the breath or the digestive fire that will not be held; the claim is the Siddhar one that holding it drives Death away. The repetition of the line with the condition reversed is the song's usual turn.

finding.claim: The idea that a fixed stock of breaths or heartbeats sets lifespan rests on a cross-species correlation; within humans, lower resting heart rate predicts lower mortality but slowing breath has not been shown to extend life.

verse.reading: While we lie on the mattress laughing with soft women, if warlike Death comes and seizes us, we too are only a dead corpse, Vaalai girl.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

tamil: பாலை இறக்கி உண்டு பசி ஒழிவது எக்காலம்?
verse.reading: When will I leave the root fire, kindle it in the hall of the moon, bring down the milk, drink it and end hunger?
verse.nuance: A cipher verse: மூலநெருப்பு is the fire at the base (kundalini), நிலா மண்டபம் the moon-hall at the crown, and பால் the nectar the tradition says drips from the moon when the fire reaches it; the hunger ended is bodily (the yogi who no longer needs food) and the soul's. Plainly it is a kitchen scene, fire moved and milk warmed, and the cipher is why it is not one.

finding.claim: Trained practitioners of breathing and cold exposure or of tummo meditation can voluntarily raise body temperature or modulate the innate immune response, effects once thought impossible.

verse.reading: They wander saying 'muppu', but they do not see the way that muppu came to be; if one turns back and says 'that is the flower', it becomes attainment, and dance.
verse.nuance: முப்பு is the Siddhars' three-salt preparation, the catalyst of their alchemy, whose identity is itself a secret of the tradition. The stanza puns on பூ: முப்பூ as three flowers and அப்பூ, 'that flower', as something turned back toward (மறித்தால்), which in the kummi's cipher is the breath turned inward; the plain and the coded readings both stand.

finding.claim: A scoping review found 220 cases of heavy-metal poisoning, mostly lead and mercury, linked to Ayurvedic and Siddha preparations, with most analysed samples over permissible limits.

verse.reading: Taking a body of eight spans, what of it, my Lord? Removing the nearness of women, there is great bliss; so that the eye may see, without the body ceasing, the knowledge that gains siddhi, the siddhi of yoga ... decree: think on it.
verse.nuance: தேகம் ஒழியாமல் சித்தி பெறும் ஞானம், the knowledge that gains siddhi without the body ceasing, is the text's statement of its goal: release in the living body. போசைவிதி is an obscure word, perhaps a corruption; the sense of the last foot is lost.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

verse.reading: Not keeping his eyes open on the tip of the nose, the poet says his body was spoiled and his understanding lost.
verse.nuance: முழித்திருந்து, staying with eyes open, makes the nose-tip gaze a waking watch and not a trance; the verse takes it as a thing to do, which Kakapusundar (2339) attacks as a false seat of the sushumna. ஆக்கை கெட்டு, the body spoiled, is the loss named for a bodily practice.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of morphometric studies reports modest structural brain differences in meditators across about eight regions, though small samples and publication bias are concerns.

verse.reading: One can remain: there is no kalpa of plant or root; in the solitary Brahman, melting, with the mind subdued, as one looks the body itself became firm; not roaming in confusion, not talking sects, not consorting with wastrels, not keeping company with the ... , see the guru's feet and bow deeply.
verse.nuance: செடிபூடு கற்பமில்லை is the plainest rejection of herbal kalpa in the work, and stands against 2353 and the formulas from 2397. கோளர் is unclear (slanderers? the planets?).

finding.claim: Ageing reflects a set of interacting cellular hallmarks such as genomic instability, loss of protein balance and stem-cell exhaustion, none yet reversed in humans.

verse.reading: Whether sitting or walking, raise the essences without letting them go through other talk; four or eight, all is one; in the good eight-limbed practice, the siddhi of practice; if you first do pranayama as the measure, by count the filling and the holding are four, the emptying one and three; without shortfall join the sarabhi and finish.

finding.claim: In two combined randomised trials, eight weeks of mindfulness training produced no structural brain changes compared with active and waitlist controls.

verse.reading: The poet says he does not know the measure of you who stood as ida and pingala and as the suzhumunai that rose, as body and as life.
verse.nuance: The three channels are named outright and the Lord is identified with them, not placed in them; எழுந்த சுழுமுனை, the whirl-channel that rose, is the middle channel the Siddhars prize, called risen because the breath rises in it. உளவு, the measure or secret, is what is unknown.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: The body is a vessel of filth; the subtle thing that comes into it, and its origin, are the matter of this Tamil song called yoga: hear it with a glad mind, jnana girl.
verse.nuance: சிற்பனம் and உற்பனம் are read as the subtle (சித்) that enters the body and its arising (உற்பத்தி); the forms are irregular. மலபாண்டம் (vessel of filth) is the stock Siddhar figure for the body, used here not to despise it but to introduce what enters it.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: Those who raised the tongue to the uvula and gazed got no result; the eyes burst and the body goes; they call it hatha yoga, and it is not fit; set the mind straight at the uvula and look: the breath subsides above and does not look downward, and one can know the uncut wheel.
verse.nuance: அடயோகம் is hatha yoga and the practice rejected is khechari mudra, the tongue turned back to the palate. Kakapusundar keeps the place and changes the instrument: the mind, not the tongue, goes to the uvula, and the breath then stays above of itself.

finding.claim: In two combined randomised trials, eight weeks of mindfulness training produced no structural brain changes compared with active and waitlist controls.

verse.reading: The fierce barbarians who roar and chase ... sink in pleasure; bewildered within the four states, when will the mind become straight, when will it know? Crores in the world hesitated; dying and being born became like a kavadi carried back and forth; drowned in sorrow, knowledge is gone; it is like knowing only in the burning ground: sheer void.
verse.nuance: The first line is corrupt (கெர்சித்துத் துரத்துச் சண்ணுஞ்) and the reading of it is a guess. நாலுபாதம் may be the four states of consciousness or the four feet (stages) of a path. The காவடி image, the pole carried back and forth on pilgrimage, makes rebirth a shuttling; சுத்தப் பாழ், the pure void, is here a verdict on wasted lives, not the yogic void.

finding.claim: A theoretical account proposes that meditation progressively loosens predictive models, from reduced mind-wandering to cessation of experience in advanced states.

verse.reading: Kin grew weary of weeping, the mourners of burning him, the mother of bearing him, and the poet of being born.
verse.nuance: Four parties are tired: the weepers, the burners, the mother, the born. உறன்முறையார், those of the proper relation, are the kin whose office it is to cremate; the stanza makes a whole lifetime out of the two ceremonies that bracket it, and 701 extends the weariness to the gods.

verse.reading: Would anyone trust this birth, my heart, while the hoard lies there and the wife is at the door, having seen, as in a dream, the hiccup, the clenched teeth, the eyes rolled up, the cotton stuffed in, and the bag choke, die and empty itself?
verse.nuance: The first of four venbas (420 to 423) on the same frame: a question to the heart about birth, then கண்டு, having seen, and a death scene. Here the scene is the deathbed itself, each symptom a word, with the cotton (பஞ்சு) stuffed in the nostrils of the corpse.

finding.claim: Reminders of death reliably shift people's attitudes and defence of their worldviews, a moderately sized effect across many studies, though recent large replications have been weaker.

verse.reading: The kundalini-breath is the letter A; at the throat of the nape is the next letter; if you place the letter M at the whirl, is this not Siva-yoga, jnana girl?
verse.nuance: The text has அகாரம் twice; the second, at the throat, must be உகாரம் (U), giving A, U and M of Om at the root, the throat and the whirl at the crown. குண்டலி வாசி joins the coiled power to the breath, as the Siddhars do: raising the breath is raising kundalini.

verse.nuance: சிற்பனம் and உற்பனம் are read as the subtle (சித்) that enters the body and its arising (உற்பத்தி); the forms are irregular. மலபாண்டம் (vessel of filth) is the stock Siddhar figure for the body, used here not to despise it but to introduce what enters it.

finding.claim: Placebos given openly, with patients told they are inert, still produce moderate improvements in self-reported symptoms.

verse.reading: You who go off driving yourselves away with 'the tattvas': if the tattva is Siva, are you not the Supreme too? After setting the root foot in nada, which is the released life, know and realise the Father within yourselves.
verse.nuance: An argument from identity: if what you call the tattvas is Siva, you who are made of them are the Supreme. முத்திசீவன் நாதம் (nada, the released life) may be in apposition or a sequence; the syntax of line 3 is loose. The verse presses toward the identity of self and Lord that later Siddhars state outright.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: Like a deer that takes a mirage for water and goes after it, fools see the life of this earth and rejoice; those who have seen the higher state do not talk empty bluster, but seek the feet of the True One; dance.
verse.nuance: The mirage-deer (கானல்மான்) closes the section on possessions by naming the error: not that wealth is bad but that it is not what it seems. மேனிலை கண்டார், those who have seen the higher state, are set against the வீம்பு (vaunting) of the world, which sits uneasily with the Siddhar's own boasts in 2005 to 2013.

finding.claim: Case reports document severe poisoning, including cerebral edema, from Siddha capsules containing arsenic, mercury and lead thousands of times above safe limits.

verse.reading: We will make a pillar appear as a small straw and a straw appear as a great pillar, we will make a man a woman and a woman a man; stand before them with a roar and dance.
verse.nuance: தோன்றிடச் செய்வோம், make it appear, admits that these are shows of appearance; the stanza's own verb puts the power on the side of illusion rather than substance. Pillar and straw correspond to the siddhis of greatness and minuteness.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.
